basis: jinshu:053:s0108 identifies 右衛督司馬雅, a distant imperial kinsman, alongside 常從督許超, both favored by the deposed crown prince. They approach 趙王倫’s adviser 孫秀 to urge action. zizhitongjian:083:s0223–s0227 names 衛督司馬雅 and 常從督許超, both former Eastern Palace attendants, plotting the prince’s restoration and making the same appeal to 孫秀. Exact full Chinese name, guard command, named associate and specific restoration plot establish one man.

The speech in jinshu:053:s0109–s0110 warns Sun Xiu that serving the empress and being thought to have known about the prince’s deposition exposes him to danger; zizhitongjian:083:s0227 gives the same warning and Sun Xiu’s agreement in s0228. These are source-framed conversations about the same deposed heir, not generic matching offices.

zizhitongjian:083:s0244 subsequently has Sun Xiu send 司馬雅 to 張華, followed by 雅’s angry reply in s0246 and departure in s0247 during the Lun/Xiu anti-Jia operation. This continued role is compatible with the initial approach and associates in Jinshu053; nothing in either complete governing frame identifies a second Sima Ya.

士猗 in Tongjian0224 is a separate named co-conspirator and is not included in this merge. The later 雅 references in0244/0246 belong to the explicitly named 司馬雅 in that passage.

The current AD300 attestation in Jinshu053 and the Tongjian deposition/coup setting are compatible; no new life date or kinship is inferred. This fresh source decision does not rehash the archived approval.
